header.name: Signals and Systems
header.description: This course introduces the concepts of continuous and discrete time signal representation, Linear Time Invariant Systems (LTI), Fourier series representation of periodic signals, continuous and discrete time Fourier transform, Laplace and Z-transforms and their application.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to classify basic signal representation; continuous time and discrete-time signals

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to determine the response of an LTI system to continuous-time or discrete-time input signals.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to represent both continuous-time and discrete-time periodic signals as Fourier series.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze continuous-time signals and systems using Fourier transform and Laplace transform.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze discrete-time signals and systems using discrete-time Fourier transform and Z-transform.

lecture_topics: Introduction: Signals - discrete and continuous time, basic representation
Classification of signals – Continuous/discrete; deterministic/random; even/odd, power, energy, periodic/aperiodic functions.
System properties – Linearity (L), time-invariance (TI), causality, memory, stability
Fourier series- for continuous time and discrete-time signal representation
system transfer function and frequency domain analysis
Solution of differential equation using unilateral Laplace transform

resources.title: Signals and Systems, 2nd Ed. by Alan V Oppenheim, Alan S Willsky and S. H. Nawab
